findings.text: `reflect.TypeOf(arg).String()` panics with a nil-pointer dereference when an argument is an untyped nil, because `reflect.TypeOf(nil)` returns a nil `reflect.Type`. The old `fmt.Sprintf("%s", ...)` printed `%!s(<nil>)` instead. For example, `Arguments{nil}.String()` now panics, and so does any mock call or diff output that formats args containing nil.
